title: Component: radio_group
description: SwiftUI Picker{.radioGroup} / WinForms RadioButton set / Compose RadioButton row. No mob equivalent. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one option selectable; selection emits a change event.

title: Screenshot over dist
description:
An agent cannot see a window today, which is why PLAN.md's rule is 'a human sees the window before CI'. Capturing the window's pixels over dist is the other half of the verification frontier.

Note the known environment boundary: a process launched from a shell detached from the GUI session cannot capture (see CLAUDE.md). Do not chase that as a bug. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Rext.Test can capture the window as an image over dist when running in a GUI session.

title: Programmatic window control from Elixir
description: close/minimize/maximize, resizable + min/max size constraints, position, save/restore geometry across launches, focus/raise, always-on-top. None exist. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Each control works from Elixir on all three backends; geometry survives a restart.

title: Rext.Style — reusable style bundles
description: mob has Mob.Style. Named, reusable prop bundles applied to nodes, so an app is not repeating six props at every call site. The composable-modifier answer that SwiftUI and Compose both landed on. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A style can be defined once and applied to multiple nodes; explicit props still win over the bundle.

title: Component: toggle (and the WinForms switch decision)
description:
SwiftUI Toggle / Compose Switch / WinForms ... nothing. Win32 has no switch control.

This is the first real test of the capability-floor rule. Two options:
  a) ship a CheckBox on Windows and accept the look
  b) owner-draw a switch

Do NOT resolve it by renaming the concept to 'checkbox' — that exports a Win32 gap to every platform permanently (tiebreak rule 5 in the nomenclature ADR). Platform-scoped props exist precisely for this. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: toggle renders as a switch on macOS/Linux; the Windows answer is decided, documented in the matrix row, and implemented.

title: Component: text_field
description:
SwiftUI TextField/SecureField / WinForms TextBox / Compose TextField. Already flagged 'Planned' in render_protocol.md.

Desktop specifics: on_focus/on_blur are load-bearing (mobile mostly is not), text selection is expected, and mob's keyboard_type prop is mobile-only — drop it. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Typing emits change events to the window; value is controlled from assigns; secure mode masks; focus/blur events fire.

title: Keyboard focus and tab order
description:
Table stakes for desktop and entirely absent: Tab/Shift-Tab traversal, a visible focus ring, programmatic focus, and a defined traversal order.

Also the prerequisite for keyboard-only operation, which is the accessibility floor on desktop. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Tab moves focus in document order, the focused node is visibly indicated, and focus can be set from Elixir.

title: ~UI sigil with :if and :for
description:
rext windows write raw nested maps. mob has ~MOB with control flow, and this is the single most visible ergonomic gap to a new user — compare the README example against mob's.

Wants: tag syntax, @assigns shorthand, :if, :for. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A window can be written with the sigil, control flow works, and the sigil compiles to the same tree the map form produces.

title: Release launcher pins REXT_PORT — only one instance can run
description:
mix rext.release's launcher hardcodes port 8137 rather than reading back the bridge's actual (possibly fallen-back) port, so a second instance cannot start.

Fix: a port-file handshake — the release writes its resolved port to a well-known file at boot, the launcher reads it before launching the renderer.

Source: rext_demo/CLAUDE.md 'Known limitation'.
acceptance_criteria: Two instances of a packaged release run simultaneously, each with its own renderer connected to the right BEAM.

title: Component: image
description: SwiftUI AsyncImage / WinForms PictureBox / Compose AsyncImage. Local and remote sources. A plain gap versus mob. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A local file and a remote URL both render on all three backends; failure to load degrades rather than crashes.

title: Window lifecycle events -> BEAM
description:
resize, move, focus, blur, and close-requested need to flow back over the protocol. None do.

close-requested is the interesting one: it has no mobile analogue at all and must be vetoable ('you have unsaved changes').

With many windows, 'which window has focus' becomes app state — it gates keyboard routing, menu contents, and close-veto. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Each event reaches the owning window process; a window can veto its own close.

title: Text selection and clipboard in fields
description: Select-all, cut/copy/paste inside text_field — expected to work with zero app code on desktop, unlike mobile where it is OS-provided in a different way. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Standard editing chords work in a focused text_field on all three backends.

title: Wire connected-backend identity from the hello frame into Rext.Platform
description:
Rext.Platform.backend/0 defaults to :compose rather than observing what actually connected. Rext.Bridge already receives a hello frame carrying a 'renderer' field — it is logged and discarded (lib/rext/bridge.ex).

Until this lands, a SwiftUI or WinForms renderer gets Compose-scoped props, so any winforms:/swiftui: scope is inert unless the app sets config :rext, :backend by hand.

Discovered while building rext-o3s.
acceptance_criteria: With a real renderer attached, Rext.Platform.backend/0 reports that backend, and backend-scoped props resolve for it without config.

title: Component: dropdown
description:
SwiftUI Picker / WinForms ComboBox / Compose ExposedDropdownMenu.

No mob equivalent — mobile uses sheets for this. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A list of options renders, selection emits a change event, and the current value is controlled from assigns.

title: Composite / reusable components
description: mob has function composites and tag composites. Without them, every app repeats trees instead of naming them. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An app can define a component once and use it in multiple windows.

title: Radius and text-size/weight design tokens
description:
Rext.Theme has 8 colors and 5 spacing steps. Missing: radius tokens (box and button both need corner_radius) and text size/weight tokens (text takes raw px only).

mob has :radius_sm/:radius_md and :base etc. Every desktop toolkit — MaterialTheme, SwiftUI Environment, XAML ResourceDictionary, GTK theme vars — has a token cascade; it is the one thing they all agree on. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: box/button accept :radius_* tokens and text accepts size/weight tokens; raw numbers still pass through.

title: Multi-window rendering (one renderer per window)
description:
THE blocking architectural gap, and the thing that most distinguishes rext from mob.

Today one renderer process draws one window, and mix rext.run launches only the app's primary window. rext_demo has a Counter and a Mirror that genuinely sync over BEAM message passing — and you can only ever see one of them.

Multi-window LOGIC is real and drivable over dist today; the rendering is not. Until this lands, rext's headline claim ('another view is another window') is unverifiable on screen. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An app declaring two windows shows two windows; both update live; closing one does not take down the other.

title: Component: box
description:
A single-child container: background, padding, corner radius, border. SwiftUI ZStack+modifiers / WinForms Panel / Compose Box+Modifier.

WinForms has no native corner radius — it needs an owner-drawn region or a platform-scoped fallback. Fill the native-mapping note before implementing.

NOTE: this issue was originally filed as 'document box, it already ships on all three backends'. That was wrong. `box` appears in all three parsers only as the DEFAULT type string for a node with no `type` field (optString("type", "box") / ?? "box"), never as a case branch. A node typed `box` falls through to the default branch and renders as a plain container.

Fold in the cleanup while here: that phantom default is misleading — an untyped node silently becomes a 'box' that isn't one. Either implement box (making the default honest) or rename the default to something that reads as 'unknown'.

Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: box renders background/padding/corner_radius on all three backends; the parsers' default type name is no longer a lie; render_protocol.md documents it.

title: Component: progress
description:
SwiftUI ProgressView / WinForms ProgressBar / Compose *ProgressIndicator.

Desktop needs determinate AND indeterminate; mob's is indeterminate-only. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Both determinate (0..1) and indeterminate modes render on all three backends.

title: Rext.Test: accessibility-tree walk
description:
mob's Mob.Test reads the AX tree for assertion-based UI testing; rext has no equivalent, so an agent can verify the BEAM-side tree but never what the backend actually rendered.

This is the cheap half of PLAN.md's 'verification frontier' — it closes the gap between 'the BEAM thinks it rendered' and 'the OS agrees', without needing screenshots or vision. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An agent can assert on the rendered native tree over dist, and a backend that silently drops a node fails the assertion.

title: Keep the component catalog in sync with the backends
description:
The catalog in render_protocol.md and the backends' type switches are maintained by hand in four places, so they can silently disagree.

Consider a test that reads the catalog table and asserts each backend handles exactly those types — a doc that is checked rather than remembered.

(Filed originally citing box as evidence of existing drift. That was a misreading: box is only the parsers' default type string, and the catalog's four types do match the backends' four branches today. The issue stands on prevention, not on an existing bug.)

Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Catalog drift fails a test rather than being noticed by a human months later.

title: Component: tabs (document tabs)
description:
SwiftUI TabView / WinForms TabControl / Compose TabRow.

NOT mob's bottom TabBar — that is a phone navigation idiom and is out of scope. This is a document tab strip. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Multiple tabs render, switching emits an event, and the active tab is controlled from assigns.

title: Component: list
description:
SwiftUI List / WinForms ListBox / Compose LazyColumn.

Desktop selection semantics have no mobile analogue: single vs multi-select, keyboard navigation, and double-click to activate. Design those in rather than porting mob's tap-only model. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Rows render from assigns, selection emits events, keyboard navigation works, double-click activates.

title: Component: checkbox
description:
SwiftUI Toggle{.checkbox} / WinForms CheckBox / Compose Checkbox.

Desktop splits checkbox from switch where mobile does not — see the toggle issue for why that split matters. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Checked/unchecked state renders and emits change events on all three backends.

title: Component: table (sortable, resizable columns)
description:
SwiftUI Table / WinForms DataGridView / Compose (hand-built).

One of the biggest 'this is a real desktop app' gaps, and entirely absent from mob. Sortable columns, resizable headers, row selection.

May subsume list and lazy_list on desktop — revisit those after this lands. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Columns render with headers, clicking a header sorts, columns resize by drag, row selection emits events.

title: Native notifications
description: UNUserNotificationCenter on macOS, toast on Windows, libnotify on Linux. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A notification posts on all three platforms and a click delivers an event to the app.

title: File dialogs: open, save, folder picker
description:
NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel on macOS, OpenFileDialog/SaveFileDialog on Windows, GtkFileChooser on Linux.

mob has a document picker (open-shaped). Save and folder-pick have no mobile analogue at all. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Each dialog opens natively and returns the chosen path(s) to the calling window.

title: Keyboard shortcuts, accelerators, and raw key events
description:
Cmd/Ctrl chords bound to actions and to menu items, plus raw keydown/keyup with modifiers.

mob has key_press/1 for its test harness but never exposed it as a user-facing API. Desktop needs the real thing. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An app can bind Cmd/Ctrl chords, they fire when the window has focus, and menu items display their binding.

title: Component: split_pane
description:
SwiftUI HSplitView/VSplitView / WinForms SplitContainer / Compose (hand-built).

User-draggable divider with a persisted ratio. Absent from mob — there is no phone analogue. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Two panes render with a draggable divider; the ratio survives a window resize and is readable from Elixir.

title: Core system integration: clipboard, open_url, alert
description: Direct ports of Mob.Clipboard, Mob.Device.open_url/1 and Mob.Alert. NSAlert / MessageBox / Compose AlertDialog for the dialog. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Clipboard round-trips text, open_url launches the default browser, and an alert blocks and returns the chosen button.

title: Rename props to the Compose/SwiftUI vocabulary
description:
Apply decisions/2026-08-08-component-nomenclature.md across the ecosystem.

  label (button) -> text
  size (text)    -> font_size
  color (text)   -> text_color
  color (button) -> background
  gap            -> spacing

Note color currently means foreground on text and background on button — same prop, opposite meaning. That is a live bug, not just a naming preference.

Touches: lib/rext/renderer.ex, native/compose, native/macos, native/windows, guides/render_protocol.md, dev/demo.exs, rext_demo, rext_new's template.

Cheap at five components, expensive at twenty-five. Do it before any new component lands.
acceptance_criteria: All three backends and all docs/examples use the new names; no occurrence of the old prop names outside the ADR; demo still renders and Rext.Test drives it.

title: Component: tree
description: SwiftUI OutlineGroup / WinForms TreeView / Compose (hand-built). Expand/collapse, nested selection. Absent from mob. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Nested nodes expand and collapse; selection emits events with the node path.

title: Drag and drop files onto a window
description: A very common desktop entry point with no mobile analogue. Dropped paths delivered to the window as an event. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Dropping one or more files on a window delivers their paths to handle_event.

title: Mouse input: right-click, double-click, hover, cursor, wheel
description:
Touch has no 'pointer is over this but not pressed' state, which is why mob marks all of this missing. Desktop cannot skip it:

  - right-click / secondary click (prerequisite for context_menu)
  - double-click (row activation)
  - hover enter/leave (prerequisite for tooltip)
  - cursor shape (pointer/text/resize)
  - scroll wheel deltas

Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Each event type reaches handle_event on all three backends with the node tag and modifiers.

title: Platform-scoped props (macos:/windows:/linux:)
description:
mob scopes props with ios:/android:. rext needs the desktop analogue:

  props: %{padding: 12, macos: %{padding: 20}}

This is the escape hatch the native-mapping rule depends on: a prop the WinForms floor cannot honor natively stays in the protocol scoped, rather than being banned outright. Without it, every capability gap becomes a vocabulary amputation.

Resolution happens in Rext.Renderer before the frame is serialized, so backends never see the scoped form. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A scoped prop resolves to the right value per backend; unscoped props are unaffected; the frame JSON contains no platform keys.

title: rext_new template: Rext.boot/1 collides with generated window tests
description:
Rext.boot/1 runs from Application.start/2 (correctly — RextDev.Boot is runtime: false, so a release relying on it opens no windows). But it also fires under MIX_ENV=test, so the app's windows hold the registered rext_window_<id> names before any test setup runs. A generated window test calling Window.start_link gets {:error, {:already_started, _}}.

Hit for real when merging rext_demo's two lineages on 2026-08-08; fixed there in the test, NOT in the generator. Every app generated by mix rext.new with a window test will hit it fresh.

Fix in rext_new's template: either an env guard or a test helper that takes over the app-booted window.
acceptance_criteria: A freshly generated app's test suite passes without hand-editing.

title: System tray / menu bar extra
description: SwiftUI MenuBarExtra / WinForms NotifyIcon / Compose Tray. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An icon appears in the tray with a working menu, and the app can run with no visible window.

title: Accessibility labels on render-tree nodes
description:
One build, two payoffs: it is the accessibility floor AND the substrate for the AX-tree walk that agents need. mob has this and rext does not.

The highest-leverage item on the board for a framework whose thesis is agent-driven development. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Every node type accepts an accessibility label; it reaches the platform AX layer on all three backends.

title: Component: scroll
description:
SwiftUI ScrollView / WinForms Panel{AutoScroll=true} / Compose verticalScroll.

Desktop needs more than mob's version: horizontal as well as vertical, plus a scrollbar visibility policy prop (desktop shows scrollbars; mobile hides them). Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Vertical and horizontal scrolling work on all three backends; content larger than the viewport is reachable.

title: dev/demo.exs looks for the renderer at a stale path
description:
dev/demo.exs probes native/macos/rext_renderer, but native/macos/build.sh produces the .app bundle (native/macos/RextRenderer.app/Contents/MacOS/rext_renderer). The demo therefore always reports 'renderer binary not found ... headless' even on a freshly built tree.

RextDev.Boot already resolves the bundle correctly and launches it via `open` — dev/demo.exs predates that and was never updated.

Discovered while verifying box/spacer/divider.
acceptance_criteria: dev/demo.exs finds a built renderer and launches it the same way RextDev.Boot does.

title: Component: divider
description: SwiftUI Divider / WinForms Label{BorderStyle=Fixed3D,Height=2} / Compose Divider. Default color :border. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A horizontal rule renders on all three backends and respects a color prop.

title: Multi-monitor and per-monitor DPI scaling
description: Per-monitor DPI on Windows is a well-known source of blurry windows when a window moves between displays. Untested on all three backends. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A window dragged between displays of different scale factors stays crisp and correctly sized.

title: Component: slider
description:
SwiftUI Slider / Compose Slider / WinForms TrackBar.

Two WinForms limits to design around: TrackBar is integer-stepped (a float value needs a scale factor) and does not support tinting. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: Dragging emits float change events within min/max on all three backends; the integer-stepping workaround is documented in the matrix row.

title: Theme cascade: light theme, system appearance, per-subtree override
description:
rext's palette is global, fixed and dark-only. The portable styling model across every desktop toolkit is tokens + per-node props with a cascade — NOT selectors (only GTK/Qt/XAML have those; SwiftUI and Compose deliberately declined).

Needs: a light palette, reading the OS color scheme (mob has Mob.Theme.color_scheme/0 + adaptive watching), user-supplied palettes, and scoping a token set to a subtree.

Explicit non-goal: a selector language. It maps onto three of six toolkits and would mean hand-rolling cascade against WinForms owner-draw. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: An app can supply its own palette, switch light/dark with the OS, and override tokens for a subtree.

title: Menu bar (app and window menus)
description:
SwiftUI Commands / WinForms MenuStrip / Compose MenuBar.

The interesting fork, and it exists ONLY because desktop has many windows: macOS has one app-level menu bar in the system bar whose contents change with the focused window; Windows puts a menu inside each window. Same Elixir declaration, structurally different model. Decide that before writing the component. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A declared menu renders in the right place per platform, items fire events, and contents track the focused window.

title: Prop validation and unknown-prop diagnostics
description:
Rext.Renderer.normalize/1 accepts any map, so a typo'd prop silently does nothing — the worst failure mode for a framework whose whole pitch is agent-driven development (an agent gets no signal it wrote the wrong name).

Validate against the catalog and surface unknown props as warnings, not crashes (forward-compat matters: an older BEAM must tolerate a newer backend's props). Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: A typo'd prop produces a warning naming the node type and the offending key; unknown *node types* still render children per the forward-compat rule.

title: Component: spacer
description:
Fixed space, or fills remaining space when no size given. SwiftUI Spacer / flex glue in WinForms.

Trivial and unblocks real layouts — the cheapest thing on the board. Source: guides/desktop_surface_matrix.md
acceptance_criteria: spacer with a size inserts it; without a size it fills; works in both row and column on all three backends.
